metadata.description: Analytics rules accompanying the Account & Credential Sharing Sentinel workbook. Generated from rules/*.yaml by src/build_rules.py - edit the YAML, not this file.
Name of the Log Analytics workspace that Microsoft Sentinel is enabled on.

properties.displayName: Account sharing - geo-velocity exceeds commercial flight
properties.description:
Two successful sign-ins for the same account whose separation in space and time
requires travelling faster than 1,500 km/h — quicker than any commercial flight,
before boarding, taxi and transit are even considered.

Distance is computed from the raw geo-coordinates on the sign-in records with
geo_distance_2points, not read from Entra ID Protection. The rule therefore works
without a P2 licence and the arithmetic is auditable: RequiredSpeedKmh, DistanceKm
and ElapsedHours all appear on the alert.

This is the single strongest sharing indicator available in sign-in telemetry.
It is not proof — a corporate VPN, a cloud egress point or a mobile carrier
backhauling traffic to a distant PoP all produce the same arithmetic. Check the
SameNetwork field and the named exclusions before escalating.
properties.query:
// --- tuning -------------------------------------------------------------
// MinSpeedKmh   raise to 2000+ to cut VPN/egress noise, lower to 900 to catch
//               slower anomalies at the cost of many more false positives.
// MinDistanceKm below ~150 km, city-level geo-IP error dominates the result.
// ExcludedUsers break-glass, scanners, backup/RMM and sanctioned kiosks.
let DetectionWindow = 1h;
let LookbackWindow  = 6h;
let MinSpeedKmh     = 1500.0;
let MinDistanceKm   = 150.0;
let ExcludedUsers   = dynamic(["none@example.invalid"]);
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackWindow)
| where ResultType == 0
| extend UserPrincipalName = tolower(UserPrincipalName)
| where isnotempty(UserPrincipalName)
| where not(UserPrincipalName has_any (ExcludedUsers))
| extend Lat     = toreal(LocationDetails.geoCoordinates.latitude),
         Lon     = toreal(LocationDetails.geoCoordinates.longitude),
         City    = tostring(LocationDetails.city),
         Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
| where isnotnull(Lat) and isnotnull(Lon)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Lat, Lon, City, Country,
          AppDisplayName, ASN = tostring(column_ifexists("AutonomousSystemNumber", "")),
          UserAgent = tostring(column_ifexists("UserAgent", ""))
| sort by UserPrincipalName asc, TimeGenerated asc
| extend pUser    = prev(UserPrincipalName), pTime = prev(TimeGenerated),
         pLat     = prev(Lat),  pLon     = prev(Lon),
         pIP      = prev(IPAddress), pCity = prev(City),
         pCountry = prev(Country), pASN   = prev(ASN)
| where pUser == UserPrincipalName
// only alert on pairs whose later sign-in landed in this run's window, so one
// violation is reported once rather than on every run for LookbackWindow
| where TimeGenerated > ago(DetectionWindow)
| extend DistanceKm   = round(geo_distance_2points(pLon, pLat, Lon, Lat) / 1000.0, 1)
| extend ElapsedHours = round(todouble(datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, pTime)) / 3600.0, 4)
| where DistanceKm > MinDistanceKm and ElapsedHours >= 0
| extend RequiredSpeedKmh = iff(ElapsedHours <= 0.0, 999999.0, round(DistanceKm / ElapsedHours, 0))
| where RequiredSpeedKmh > MinSpeedKmh
| extend Verdict = case(RequiredSpeedKmh > 5000, "Physically impossible - concurrent use or proxy",
                        "Impossible without a flight - very likely shared")
| extend SameNetwork = iff(isnotempty(ASN) and ASN == pASN, "Yes - single ASN, suspect VPN or carrier egress", "No")
| extend AccountName      = tostring(split(UserPrincipalName, "@")[0]),
         AccountUPNSuffix = tostring(split(UserPrincipalName, "@")[1])
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AccountName, AccountUPNSuffix, Verdict,
          RequiredSpeedKmh, DistanceKm, ElapsedHours, SameNetwork,
          FromCity = pCity, FromCountry = pCountry, FromIP = pIP,
          ToCity = City, ToCountry = Country, ToIP = IPAddress,
          AppDisplayName, UserAgent, ASN
| sort by RequiredSpeedKmh desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat:
{{UserPrincipalName}} signed in from {{FromCity}}, {{FromCountry}} ({{FromIP}}) and then from
{{ToCity}}, {{ToCountry}} ({{ToIP}}) — {{DistanceKm}} km apart in {{ElapsedHours}} hours,
requiring {{RequiredSpeedKmh}} km/h. Single-ASN path: {{SameNetwork}}.

properties.displayName: Account sharing - session or refresh token used from more than one country
properties.description:
A single token identifier (UniqueTokenIdentifier) presented successfully from
IP addresses that geo-locate to more than one country.

A token is bound to a session, not to a person. The same token appearing in two
countries means the token itself moved — either lifted by an adversary-in-the-middle
proxy and replayed, or deliberately handed to a second person along with the
session. Both are worth an incident; the tradecraft and the arrangement are
indistinguishable from the telemetry alone.

Unlike a password-based sign-in, this cannot be explained by two people knowing
the same secret and authenticating independently — that would mint two distinct
tokens. One token, two countries, is a narrower and stronger finding.

Known benign causes: a mobile device roaming across a border mid-session, and
split-tunnel VPN clients that change egress country without re-authenticating.
properties.query:
// --- tuning -------------------------------------------------------------
// MinCountries  2 is the intended setting. Raising it defeats the purpose.
// LookbackWindow widen to 24h to catch slow replay, at the cost of re-alerting
//               on long-lived tokens until suppression catches up.
let DetectionWindow = 1h;
let LookbackWindow  = 6h;
let MinCountries    = 2;
let ExcludedUsers   = dynamic(["none@example.invalid"]);
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackWindow)
| where ResultType == 0
| where isnotempty(UniqueTokenIdentifier)
| extend UserPrincipalName = tolower(UserPrincipalName)
| where isnotempty(UserPrincipalName)
| where not(UserPrincipalName has_any (ExcludedUsers))
| extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion),
         City    = tostring(LocationDetails.city)
| summarize Countries   = dcountif(Country, isnotempty(Country)),
            IPs         = dcount(IPAddress),
            ASNs        = dcountif(tostring(AutonomousSystemNumber), isnotempty(tostring(AutonomousSystemNumber))),
            CountryList = make_set_if(Country, isnotempty(Country), 10),
            CityList    = make_set_if(City, isnotempty(City), 10),
            IPList      = make_set(IPAddress, 15),
            Apps        = make_set(AppDisplayName, 10),
            TokenType   = any(tostring(column_ifexists("IncomingTokenType", ""))),
            Uses        = count(),
            FirstUse    = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastUse     = max(TimeGenerated)
    by UserPrincipalName, UniqueTokenIdentifier
| where Countries >= MinCountries
// only surface tokens still in active use during this run's window
| where LastUse > ago(DetectionWindow)
| extend SpanMinutes = round(todouble(datetime_diff('second', LastUse, FirstUse)) / 60.0, 1)
| extend Assessment = case(Countries >= 3, "One token presented from three or more countries - replay is the only sane explanation",
                           "One token presented from two countries - AiTM token theft or a deliberately shared session")
| extend AccountName      = tostring(split(UserPrincipalName, "@")[0]),
         AccountUPNSuffix = tostring(split(UserPrincipalName, "@")[1]),
         SampleIP         = tostring(IPList[0])
| project TimeGenerated = LastUse, UserPrincipalName, AccountName, AccountUPNSuffix,
          Assessment, Countries, IPs, ASNs, Uses, SpanMinutes, TokenType,
          UniqueTokenIdentifier, CountryList, CityList, IPList, Apps, FirstUse, LastUse, SampleIP
| sort by Countries desc, Uses desc

properties.description:
Any authentication attempt involving a honeytoken account — success or failure,
cloud or on-premises.

A honeytoken is a decoy identity that no person, script or service has any
legitimate reason to touch. It is the only zero-false-positive signal in the
Account and Credential Sharing workbook: a hit means someone enumerated the
directory, harvested a credential store, or was handed a list of accounts.
There is no benign explanation to rule out first.

Three sources are covered:
  * accounts named explicitly in HoneytokenAccounts below
  * identities tagged as honeytokens in Defender for Identity
  * Defender for Identity's own honeytoken alerts

IMPORTANT: this rule does nothing until you either tag honeytoken accounts in
Defender for Identity (Settings > Identities > Entity tags > Honeytoken) or list
them in HoneytokenAccounts. An empty result here means none are configured — which
is itself the finding, and the cheapest detection win available.

Deliberately fires on failures as well as successes. A failed honeytoken logon is
an attacker guessing, and is just as interesting as a successful one.
properties.query:
// --- tuning -------------------------------------------------------------
// HoneytokenAccounts  list every decoy account, lowercase. Match is on the
//   account name (SAM) or the full UPN, so either form works. Leave the
//   placeholder in place and the rule relies solely on MDI honeytoken tagging.
let DetectionWindow     = 15m;
let HoneytokenAccounts  = dynamic([
    "ht-domainadmin-backup"
]);
let isHoneytoken = (name: string, upn: string)
{
    tolower(name) in (HoneytokenAccounts) or tolower(upn) in (HoneytokenAccounts)
};
union isfuzzy=true
  (SigninLogs
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(DetectionWindow)
     | extend UserPrincipalName = tolower(UserPrincipalName)
     | extend SamName = tostring(split(UserPrincipalName, "@")[0])
     | where isHoneytoken(SamName, UserPrincipalName)
     | project TimeGenerated,
               Source     = "Entra ID sign-in",
               Account    = UserPrincipalName,
               Outcome    = iff(ResultType == 0, "Success", strcat("Failure (", tostring(ResultType), ")")),
               Detail     = strcat(ClientAppUsed, " / ", AppDisplayName),
               Host       = tostring(DeviceDetail.displayName),
               IPAddress  = IPAddress,
               Location   = strcat(tostring(LocationDetails.city), ", ", tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion))),
  (IdentityLogonEvents
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(DetectionWindow)
     | extend AccountUpnLower = tolower(coalesce(AccountUpn, strcat(AccountName, "@", AccountDomain)))
     | where isHoneytoken(AccountName, AccountUpnLower)
           or tostring(AdditionalFields) has "oneytoken"
     | project TimeGenerated,
               Source     = "On-prem AD (MDI)",
               Account    = AccountUpnLower,
               Outcome    = ActionType,
               Detail     = strcat(coalesce(LogonType, ""), " ", coalesce(Protocol, "")),
               Host       = coalesce(DeviceName, TargetDeviceName),
               IPAddress  = IPAddress,
               Location   = coalesce(Location, "")),
  (IdentityDirectoryEvents
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(DetectionWindow)
     | extend AccountUpnLower = tolower(coalesce(AccountUpn, strcat(AccountName, "@", AccountDomain))),
              TargetUpnLower  = tolower(coalesce(TargetAccountUpn, ""))
     | where isHoneytoken(AccountName, AccountUpnLower)
           or isHoneytoken(TargetAccountDisplayName, TargetUpnLower)
           or tostring(AdditionalFields) has "oneytoken"
     | project TimeGenerated,
               Source     = "On-prem AD directory activity (MDI)",
               Account    = coalesce(iff(isempty(TargetUpnLower), "", TargetUpnLower), AccountUpnLower),
               Outcome    = ActionType,
               Detail     = coalesce(Protocol, ""),
               Host       = coalesce(DeviceName, DestinationDeviceName),
               IPAddress  = IPAddress,
               Location   = coalesce(Location, "")),
  (SecurityAlert
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(DetectionWindow)
     | where AlertName has "oneytoken"
     | project TimeGenerated,
               Source     = "Defender for Identity alert",
               Account    = tolower(tostring(CompromisedEntity)),
               Outcome    = AlertName,
               Detail     = Description,
               Host       = "",
               IPAddress  = "",
               Location   = "")
| where isnotempty(Account)
| extend AccountName      = tostring(split(Account, "@")[0]),
         AccountUPNSuffix = tostring(split(Account, "@")[1])
| extend Assessment = "Honeytoken touched - no legitimate process authenticates as this identity. Treat as credential harvesting or directory enumeration until proven otherwise."
| project TimeGenerated, Account, AccountName, AccountUPNSuffix, Source, Outcome,
          Assessment, Detail, Host, IPAddress, Location
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

properties.displayName: Account sharing - generic or service account interactive logon from a new host
properties.description:
An account whose name matches the generic/service naming pattern (svc-, shared-,
admin-, training-, kiosk-, scanner- and similar) performs an interactive logon
from a host it has never been seen on in the preceding 14 days.

Two things make this interesting together. A genuine service account should not
log on interactively at all — it should authenticate as a service, a batch job or
an application. And an account with no real owner spreading to a new endpoint is
how a shared credential propagates through an organisation: someone needed it,
someone else gave it to them, and now it lives on another machine.

The 14-day baseline is what keeps this quiet. A service account that has always
run interactively from the same two jump boxes never fires. The alert is the
change, not the condition.

Accounts with no baseline activity at all are deliberately excluded — a newly
created account's first logon is provisioning, not spread. It will alert on its
second distinct host instead.
properties.query:
// --- tuning -------------------------------------------------------------
// BaselineWindow  shorten to 7d in a fast-moving estate; anything under 7d
//                 starts alerting on normal rotation between jump boxes.
// GenericRx       trim terms that are legitimate naming convention in your
//                 tenant before you tune anything else, or you will tune
//                 thresholds around noise you could have deleted.
let DetectionWindow = 1h;
let BaselineWindow  = 14d;
let GenericRx = @"(?i)(^|[._\-])(svc|service|shared|generic|common|team|group|dept|admin|administrator|adm|test|tst|temp|tmp|training|train|demo|kiosk|lobby|frontdesk|reception|scanner|scan|printer|print|copier|fax|conf|conference|room|guest|intern|contractor|vendor|support|helpdesk|sql|oracle|backup|batch|task|sched|robot|bot|rpa|automation|integration|api|app|monitor|nagios|zabbix|splunk|jenkins|build|deploy)([._\-]|[0-9]|@|$)";
let ExcludedUsers = dynamic(["none@example.invalid"]);
let logons = materialize(
    union isfuzzy=true
      (SigninLogs
         | where TimeGenerated > ago(BaselineWindow)
         | where ResultType == 0
         | extend UserPrincipalName = tolower(UserPrincipalName)
         | extend Host = tostring(DeviceDetail.displayName)
         | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, Host,
                   Source    = "Entra interactive",
                   LogonKind = strcat(ClientAppUsed, " / ", AppDisplayName),
                   IPAddress = IPAddress,
                   Location  = strcat(tostring(LocationDetails.city), ", ", tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion))),
      (IdentityLogonEvents
         | where TimeGenerated > ago(BaselineWindow)
         | where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
         | where LogonType in ("Interactive", "Remote interactive")
         | extend UserPrincipalName = tolower(coalesce(AccountUpn, strcat(AccountName, "@", AccountDomain)))
         | extend Host = coalesce(DeviceName, TargetDeviceName)
         | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, Host,
                   Source    = "On-prem AD (MDI)",
                   LogonKind = LogonType,
                   IPAddress = IPAddress,
                   Location  = coalesce(Location, ""))
    | where isnotempty(UserPrincipalName) and isnotempty(Host)
    | where not(UserPrincipalName has_any (ExcludedUsers))
    | where UserPrincipalName matches regex GenericRx
);
let baseline = logons
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(BaselineWindow) .. ago(DetectionWindow))
    | summarize BaselineLogons = count() by UserPrincipalName, Host;
// accounts that actually have a history - a brand new account's first logon is
// provisioning, not spread, so it should not raise an incident
let establishedAccounts = baseline
    | summarize KnownHosts = dcount(Host), HostList = make_set(Host, 25) by UserPrincipalName;
logons
| where TimeGenerated > ago(DetectionWindow)
| join kind=leftanti baseline on UserPrincipalName, Host
| join kind=inner establishedAccounts on UserPrincipalName
| summarize TimeGenerated  = max(TimeGenerated),
            FirstSeenHere  = min(TimeGenerated),
            Logons         = count(),
            LogonKinds     = make_set(LogonKind, 6),
            IPAddress      = any(IPAddress),
            Location       = any(Location),
            Source         = any(Source),
            KnownHosts     = any(KnownHosts),
            PreviousHosts  = any(HostList)
    by UserPrincipalName, Host
| extend Assessment = case(KnownHosts >= 5, strcat("Generic account already seen on ", tostring(KnownHosts), " hosts has reached another - this credential is circulating"),
                           KnownHosts >= 2, "Generic account spreading to an additional host - verify who was given it and why",
                           "Generic account has left its usual host for the first time")
| extend AccountName      = tostring(split(UserPrincipalName, "@")[0]),
         AccountUPNSuffix = tostring(split(UserPrincipalName, "@")[1])
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AccountName, AccountUPNSuffix, Host,
          Assessment, Source, Logons, LogonKinds, KnownHosts, PreviousHosts,
          IPAddress, Location, FirstSeenHere
| sort by KnownHosts desc, TimeGenerated desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Generic account {{UserPrincipalName}} logged on interactively from new host {{Host}}

properties.displayName: Account sharing - one MFA factor newly registered against a third account
properties.description:
A single authentication factor — a phone number, an email address or an
authenticator device — becomes bound to a third distinct account, with the
registration that crossed that threshold occurring in this detection window.

Two accounts sharing a recovery factor is common and usually benign: an
administrator with a separate privileged identity, or a contractor with a second
tenant account. Three is where the explanation stops being tidy. A factor
registered against three or more identities means one person can complete
multi-factor authentication for all of them, or that one phone is the recovery
path for a set of accounts that are supposed to be independent.

This is the control-plane version of account sharing. It does not require anyone
to have shared a password — whoever holds the factor can reset their way into
every account bound to it.

PRIVACY NOTE: the alert carries the factor value, which may be a personal phone
number or email address. That is what makes the alert actionable, but it means
these incidents inherit the sensitivity of the directory. Restrict access to the
incident accordingly.

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat:
A single {{MethodType}} is now registered as an authentication factor against {{AccountsSharing}}
distinct accounts, the most recent being {{UserPrincipalName}}. {{Assessment}} Whoever holds
this factor can complete multi-factor authentication, or drive account recovery, for every
account bound to it.

properties.displayName: Account sharing - local administrator authenticating over the network to many hosts
properties.description:
A local (non-domain) account with local administrator rights authenticates over
the network to five or more distinct devices within an hour.

A local account is, by definition, local. It exists in the SAM database of one
machine. When the same local administrator name and secret authenticates across
a fleet, only one thing is happening: that password is identical on every one of
those machines, and somebody — an administrator, a deployment image, or an
attacker who dumped it once — is using that fact.

This is the precondition for classic lateral movement. It is also the single
most common finding in environments that have not deployed LAPS, where a build
image set the same local administrator password on every endpoint years ago and
nobody has changed it since.

Distinguishing benign from malicious: a scheduled management sweep hits the same
target list at the same time every day and comes from one source host. Credential
reuse by an operator or an adversary looks irregular, comes from a workstation,
and often follows a credential-dumping alert. The SourceHosts and LogonTypes
fields are what tell them apart.

If the finding is benign, the remediation is still the same: deploy LAPS, or
Windows LAPS in Entra, so the password is unique per device.

Grouping note: the rule keys on the account NAME alone. A local account's domain
component is the machine it lives on, and its SID is machine-specific, so keying
on either would place every host in its own bucket and the fan-out could never
appear. The distinct-SID count is reported instead as corroboration — more than
one SID confirms these are genuinely separate SAM accounts sharing a name.
